zotero.abstractNote: Contact modeling is a cornerstone of robotics, enabling the simulation and control of robots interacting with their environment. Complementarity-based models have emerged as a powerful framework for representing contact, friction, and impact, providing a mathematically rigorous foundation for handling the non-smooth nature of these phenomena. This tutorial provides a comprehensive overview of complementarity-based contact models, covering their mathematical formulation, numerical solution methods, and their application in robotics. We discuss the transition from classical rigid-body dynamics to complementarity systems, detail the formulation of the Linear Complementarity Problem (LCP) and its extensions, and review state-of-the-art solvers. Finally, we highlight current challenges and future directions in the field.
